# requireString

<link-summary>Returns the value as a string, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireString() — Returns the value as a string, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireString(value: unknown, message?: string): string;
```

The test is `typeof value === "string"`, so the empty string passes and a `String` object, being an object, does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a string.

## Throws

| Exception                | Condition                  |
| :----------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `InvalidStringException` | the value is not a string. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireString(""); // => ""
requireString("abc"); // => "abc"
requireString(1); // throws InvalidStringException
requireString(null); // throws InvalidStringException
```
